Candidate A changes the required API and introduces explicitly forbidden scope.","reasons":["B preserves the required Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) API; A instead exposes opts ...AddFileOption.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile exactly as required, while A adds unnecessary NewFileWithFields machinery.","A adds association-field options despite the contract explicitly prohibiting association fields and changing FilesOption behavior.","A modifies global RawClient retry/body behavior, contrary to the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery. Its makeBodyReplayable also silently ignores io.ReadAll failures after potentially consuming part of the request body, risking corrupted requests and lost source-reader errors firmly required to propagate—not silently disappear into a non-replayable/partially consumed request body..@#? Better sentence no weirdness."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add and duplicates its request construction, response decoding, and error semantics.","The globally applied replay buffering can unexpectedly consume and retain every non-replayable request body in memory.","makeBodyReplayable discards read errors and may leave req.Body partially consumed, producing an incorrect first request as well as no useful source-reader error."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the extracted private add helper rather than routing through the public FilesService.Add method as explicitly required.","The added tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, despite the contract requiring those cases.","Buffering inside Add changes when the source is read and wraps reader errors, which may be a subtle behavior change even though it directly enables retries for existing Add callers."]}
